# Wall 1 second read and ruling — A.23 × C.2.c

**Generated by:** `source/build/goldset/239_a23_wall1_ruling.py` from `extraction/co-residence-parents-household-delay-wall1-adjudication.json`

**Ticket:** TICK-075 · **Read:** 2026-08-28 · **Reader:** Shravan

## 1. The dispute is a seventh the size it looked

`231` assembled 26 records and stated three positions. The packet was built on **exposure** — everything where a price and the living arrangement move together — which is the right net for a boundary dispute and the wrong basis for counting one. Sorted on what each record actually **estimates**, it falls apart:

| Outcome estimated | n | What that means |
|---|---|---|
| `FERTILITY` | 8 | a birth, a parity progression or completed fertility is the dependent variable |
| `INTENTION` | 1 | a stated fertility intention — pooled separately under the standing D.3.b rule |
| `ARRANGEMENT` | 6 | **the living arrangement is the dependent variable** — link 1 of the chain, and not a fertility estimate under any ruling |
| `PRICE` | 1 | a price is the estimated object |
| `REVERSE` | 1 | fertility acts on housing — the reverse channel, threat 1 |
| `NO_ESTIMATE` | 8 | framing, typology or policy description; nothing is estimated |
| `UNRESOLVED` | 1 | the available record does not support a classification |

**8 of the 26 estimate nothing at all** and **6 have the arrangement itself as the dependent variable.** The second group is the important one, and it includes two of the packet's most-cited members — the JEEA mortgage-cost paper and Acolin, Lin & Wachter. Fertility appears in their motivation and not in their estimation. **No ruling about ownership can turn a link-1 record into a fertility estimate**, so they leave the dispute whichever way the wall is drawn.

What is genuinely contested is **8 records — 7 distinct studies**, once the Spanish subsidy's preprint and published version are counted once, **of which 3 are identified**.

## 2. The ruling

> **Ruling 3 — shared and non-additive, and the sub-ruling stands. (Shravan, 2026-08-28; PI confirmation pending.)**
> Position 3 of the three `231` set out. The records classified `SHARED` below are reported in both chapters, flagged `MIXED_PRICE_ARRANGEMENT`, and **neither chapter claims their magnitude alone**. Both demographic-significance sections must say so in terms, because the failure this prevents is double-counting the same effect in two chapters of one review.
>
> **Why not strict inheritance (position 1).** It would take the identified core out of A.23 and leave the chapter reporting that its registered claim has almost no identified evidence — a conclusion produced by a filing decision rather than by the literature. The same objection Ruling 1 raised against dropping the extended arm.
>
> **Why not target-based (position 2).** It would give A.23 the identified core outright and oblige C.2.c — a finished chapter — to hand back records it has already read and rated. It also requires the review to decide a policy's *target*, which is a claim about legislative intent and not about variation.
>
> **What makes position 3 cheap here, and this is new.** It was the expensive option when the packet looked like 26 contested records. At 8 it costs both chapters a shared paragraph and one flag. The measurement that made the ruling easy is the one `231` did not run.

## 3. What the contested records are

**Subsidized Housing and the Transition to Adulthood** · `identified` · reported by A.23 **and** C.2.c, magnitude claimed alone by neither

  Administrative allocation of subsidised dwellings against how and when children become adults, fertility among the outcomes. Design 3 in a peer-reviewed demography journal. The treatment is a housing programme; the target is the arrangement. Genuinely mixed.

**Waking Up from the American Dream** · `identified` · reported by A.23 **and** C.2.c, magnitude claimed alone by neither

  THE DECOMPOSITION RECORD. One instrument (predetermined industrial structure) and three outcomes estimated jointly -- home ownership, household formation, fertility. It is the only design in the frame that can say how much of a price effect on fertility travels through household formation. Both chapters must report it; neither can claim its magnitude alone.

**Fostering Household Formation: Evidence from a Spanish Rental Subsidy** · `identified` · reported by A.23 **and** C.2.c, magnitude claimed alone by neither

  THE ARCHETYPAL MIXED CASE the sub-ruling was written for. A cash subsidy conditional on renting -- a price change whose eligibility condition IS establishing an independent residence -- with living apart from parents, partnering AND childbearing as outcomes. Published version; keep over the preprint.

**Fostering the Emancipation of Young People (SSRN preprint)** · `identified` · reported by A.23 **and** C.2.c, magnitude claimed alone by neither

  Preprint of the record above. One study, two records. Retrieved at 5e; the published version is not. Read the preprint, cite the published version, record the version used.

**Do housing options affect child birth decisions? Evidence from Taiwan** · `observational` · reported by A.23 **and** C.2.c, magnitude claimed alone by neither

  THE BEST EMPIRICAL ADJUDICATOR IN THE PACKET. The Taiwan PSFD option set spans renting, owning, living with parents or siblings, living in a house bought by parents, and staff housing, against a birth outcome. Tenure and the arrangement enter ONE choice set, so the two variables can be read against each other instead of assigned by ruling. Observational, so it settles the descriptive question and not the causal one.

**LIVING ARRANGEMENT AND HOMEOWNERSHIP IMPACTS ON FERTILITY INTENTION** · `observational` · reported by A.23 **and** C.2.c, magnitude claimed alone by neither

  Both Wall 1 variables in one ordinal logit, Indonesia. Outcome is a stated INTENTION, so it pools separately under the standing D.3.b rule and cannot carry a realized-fertility verdict.

**Childbearing Behavior in the Light of Different Housing Regimes: First Births in Sweden 1975-2004** · `observational` · reported by A.23 **and** C.2.c, magnitude claimed alone by neither

  Thirty years of Swedish first births against housing regime, register-grade. The exposure is a regime rather than isolated variation in either variable.

**The trifecta of adulthood: Housing, partnering and childbearing trajectories** · `observational` · reported by A.23 **and** C.2.c, magnitude claimed alone by neither

  Sequence analysis of adulthood pathways in East Asia; all three elements as one trajectory object. Descriptive of the joint distribution, which is what it is useful for -- it cannot separate the two variables either.

## 5. What this read does not settle

- **It is one reader, and the same reader who screened.** A consistency read, not a panel. The standing rule that adversarial re-rating by one rater is not independence applies to a boundary read exactly as it applies to a GRADE rating.
- **It does not settle who *should* own the contested records**, which is what `231` said reading them could not do. It settles that the question is smaller, and it takes the option that costs least on the reduced set.
- **1 record remains unclassified** and is named rather than assigned. Two more were classified from a title and a screen note because retrieval did not reach them, and they are flagged in the source file.
- **The Taiwan PSFD record is the empirical adjudicator and it is observational.** It puts tenure and the arrangement in one choice set against a birth outcome, so it can show how the two variables behave together. It cannot show which one causes what.
